title: Tax is calculated on the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the 5% discount is applied but tax is still 10% of the undiscounted subtotal, so every discounted order is overcharged.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with 80 x p-102 (unit 12.50), subtotal 100000 cents (see evidence/api/rules-T2.json)
Observe tax_cents 10000 and total_cents 105000
UI: Client Portal as acme-1 > New order, reference QA-ui-order-1, Ballpoint Pens x 80, Place order: confirmation says Total $1,050.00 and the order page shows Tax $100.00
actual: discount 5000, tax 10000, total 105000. Same error for 154 x p-101 (tax 10010 vs 9510) and a multi-line order (10989 vs 10439). Orders below 1000.00 are correct.
suspected_cause: Tax computed from subtotal rather than subtotal - discount

regression_test.description: Order with subtotal 100000 expects tax 9500 and total 104500

plain.title: Customers with discounted orders are charged too much tax
plain.where: Client Portal → New order, and every order page
plain.what_happens: When an order is $1,000 or more, the 5% discount is given but tax is still worked out on the price before the discount. An $1,000 order shows a total of $1,050.00 instead of $1,045.00.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer placing an order of $1,000 or more, and staff reading those totals and the sales figures.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer.
Type a reference such as QA-test, choose Ballpoint Pens, box of 50, and set the quantity to 80.
The green message says Total: $1,050.00. Open the order: Subtotal $1,000.00, Discount -$50.00, Tax $100.00.
plain.expected: Tax should be $95.00 and the total $1,045.00.

title: Any customer can read every company's customer records, including personal and card details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns 200 with all customer records for client roles; the spec says admin only.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 (a client) over the API
GET /api/admin/customers (evidence/api/recon-R2.json)
Observe 200 with contact details, ID numbers, addresses and card details of all companies; zain-1 gets the same (evidence/api/rules-A1.json)
actual: 200 with all customers' records. One record's notes also contain a full card number.
suspected_cause: Admin role check missing on the customers route (reports route does check)

plain.title: Any customer can see other companies' private contact and payment details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: A signed-in customer can retrieve the full customer list, which holds other companies' names, phone numbers, addresses, ID numbers and card details. The screens hide this, but the system does not refuse it.
plain.who_is_affected: All customers, whose private details are exposed to every other customer.
plain.expected: Customers are refused; only staff can see this list.

title: A customer can open another company's order
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns 200 for an order owned by a different company; the spec requires 404.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API and POST /api/orders (reference QA-iso)
Sign in as bright-1 (Bright Foods) and GET /api/orders/{that id} (evidence/api/rules-X3.json); zain-1 same (rules-X4.json)
Observe 200 with the order
UI: sign in to the Client Portal as bright-1 and open order.html?id=o-1042 (an Acme order): the order page is shown
actual: 200 and full order details. The order list and search are correctly filtered, only direct access leaks.
suspected_cause: Detail lookup does not compare the order's company with the caller's company

regression_test.description: Client of company B reading company A's order expects 404

plain.title: A customer can view another company's orders by changing the address
plain.where: Client Portal → My orders → an order page
plain.what_happens: If a customer of Company B opens the address of a Company A order, the full order is shown. The orders list is filtered correctly, but the direct address is not protected.
plain.who_is_affected: All customers; each company's orders can be read by every other company.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer of Company A, open an order and note the number at the end of the address bar.
Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer of Company B (use a fresh browser window).
Type the Company A order address into the address bar, keeping the same number at the end.
You see Company A's order details.
plain.expected: Company B should be told the order does not exist.

title: Signing out does not end the session on the server
summary: After POST /auth/logout returns 204 the same token is still accepted.
steps: Sign in as zain-1 over the API
POST /api/auth/logout: 204
GET /api/me and GET /api/orders with the same token (evidence/api/rules-O2.json, rules-O3.json)
Observe 200 on both
expected: 401 as soon as the user signs out (spec and business rule)
suspected_cause: Logout does not add the token to a revocation list

regression_test.description: After logout the same token on GET /me expects 401

plain.title: Signing out does not actually end the session
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: After someone signs out, their old sign-in is still accepted by the system. The sign-out button takes them to the sign-in page, but anyone holding the old sign-in can keep working.
plain.who_is_affected: Every user of both portals, especially on shared computers.
plain.expected: Signing out ends the session at once.

title: Orders with zero, negative, fractional or oversized quantities, or no items, are accepted
summary: POST /orders accepts items:[] and quantities 0, -1, 1001 and 1.5 with HTTP 201; the negative quantity gives a negative total.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with items[0].quantity=-1 (evidence/api/rules-V1.json)
Observe 201 and a negative total; also quantity 0, 1001, 1.5 and empty items (client-base-P043..P046)
expected: 400 naming the field; quantity must be a whole number 1 to 1000 and at least one item
actual: 201 for all. The order list shows -$7.15 for a negative order and the sales report counts it.
suspected_cause: No range or integer check on quantity and no minimum item count

regression_test.description: Quantities -1, 0, 1001, 1.5 and empty items each expect 400

plain.title: The system accepts impossible orders, such as minus one item or no items
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: An order for a negative or zero number of items, more than 1,000 of one item, or with no items at all is accepted and saved. A negative order shows a negative total and distorts sales figures.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers and staff reading order totals; the company's sales figures.
plain.expected: These orders are refused with a clear message.

title: Error answers reveal internal technical details (file locations and code traces)
summary: Malformed JSON to POST /auth/login and POST /orders returns a stack trace with server file paths in the error body.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with raw body {"broken": (evidence/api/client-base-P007.json)
Observe 400 with an error.trace field holding a stack trace and absolute file paths
Same for POST /api/orders (client-base-P048.json)
expected: A short error without internals (spec: responses never include stack traces or file paths)
actual: error.trace contains the stack and server file paths

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON response has no trace field

plain.title: Error messages expose the system's internal workings
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When the system receives a malformed request it answers with internal technical details and the location of files on the server, which helps an attacker.
plain.who_is_affected: The company's security; not visible to normal users.
plain.expected: Only a short, plain error message is returned.

title: Some order list requests crash the server or ignore limits
summary: GET /orders with page_size=0, q=( or q=\ returns HTTP 500; page_size=-1 returns 200 with page_size -1.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 (evidence/api/client-base-P019.json): 500
GET /api/orders?q=( and ?q=\ (P024, P028): 500
GET /api/orders?page_size=-1 (P020): 200
expected: 400 for invalid values; searches with punctuation return normal results
actual: 500 on three inputs; page_size=-1 accepted, against the documented 1 to 100
suspected_cause: Unvalidated page_size and the search text used as a regular expression

plain.title: Searching with certain characters in the orders list makes the system fail
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal and Admin Portal)
plain.what_happens: Typing a bracket or backslash into order search, or asking for zero orders per page, makes the system fail with an error instead of showing results.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff and customers who search orders using such characters.
plain.expected: Searches work normally and invalid page sizes are refused politely.

title: Placing the same order twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical POST /orders sent in parallel both return 201 and are stored. The spec does not say duplicates must be refused, so intent is uncertain.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
Send the same POST /orders twice at once (evidence/api/client-base-P049.json)
Observe two 201 responses and two orders
expected: Probably one order, or a duplicate warning (not specified)

regression_test.description: Two parallel identical orders: decide and assert the intended behaviour

plain.title: A double click on Place order may create two identical orders
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When the same order is sent twice at the same moment, two orders are created. It is not stated whether this is intended; we did not check a double click on the screen.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers who double click, and staff handling duplicates.
plain.expected: One order is created, or the customer is warned.

title: New order page does not fit a phone screen; Place order button is off screen
summary: At 390px wide the page is 555px wide; reference, note, quantity, Remove and Place order sit beyond the right edge, and Remove is covered by the quantity box.
steps: Fresh profile, sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Set viewport 390x844
Open New order
Observe the fields cut off at the right edge and Place order starting at x=435 of 390
Reload: same (scrollWidth 555)
expected: All fields and the Place order button are visible without sideways scrolling
actual: Page scrolls sideways; the Place order button is hidden off screen
suspected_cause: Fixed minimum widths on the form row

regression_test.description: At 390px width page scrollWidth equals viewport width

plain.title: On a phone, the New order form is cut off and the Place order button is out of view
plain.what_happens: On a narrow screen the form is wider than the screen, so the fields are cut off and the Place order button is off to the right, hard to find.
how_to_see_it: Open the Client Portal on a phone, or make the browser window very narrow.
Sign in as a customer and click New order.
The text boxes run past the right edge and Place order is not visible without sliding the page sideways.
plain.expected: The whole form fits the screen.

title: Urdu company names are shown back to front in the Admin Portal
summary: Cells with Urdu text have unicode-bidi: bidi-override with direction ltr, so the letters appear in reverse order and unjoined.
steps: Sign in to the Admin Portal as admin
Open Orders: the client for Zain's orders reads reversed (screenshots/admin-orders-desktop.png)
Open Reports, wait about 5 seconds: Sales by client shows the same reversed name (admin-reports-loaded-desktop.png)
Inspect: the cell text is the correct string but computed unicode-bidi is bidi-override
expected: The name displays correctly right to left
actual: The name is displayed with letters reversed
suspected_cause: A text-cell style forces bidi-override ltr

regression_test.description: Urdu client name cell must not use bidi-override

plain.title: Urdu customer names appear reversed and broken in the Admin Portal
plain.where: Admin Portal → Orders, Customers and Reports
plain.what_happens: The Urdu company name is displayed back to front with its letters not joined, so staff cannot read it correctly.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff dealing with the Urdu-language customer.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Admin Portal.
Click Orders and find an order from the Urdu customer.
Look at the Client column: the Urdu name reads back to front.
Click Reports: the same name in Sales by client is also reversed.

title: Sales report is slow and shows only a spinner for about four seconds
summary: GET /admin/reports/sales takes about 4.0 seconds every time; the Reports page shows a spinner meanwhile.
steps: Sign in as admin over the API
GET /api/admin/reports/sales (evidence/api/recon-R4.json)
Observe about 4000 ms, repeatably
suspected_cause: Artificial delay or an unindexed aggregation

plain.title: The Reports page takes about four seconds to show its figures
plain.what_happens: After opening Reports, only the heading and a spinner appear for around four seconds before the figures show.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Admin Portal.
A spinner shows under Sales summary for about four seconds before the figures appear.

title: Admin order search and icon buttons have no accessible names
summary: The search box has only a placeholder, and the refresh and clear buttons are icons with no text, label or title.
steps: Sign in to the Admin Portal as admin
Open Orders
Run the page audit: unnamedControls lists input#search, button#refresh, button#clear-filters (also at 390px)
expected: Each control has an accessible name

regression_test.description: Controls on the orders page have accessible names

plain.title: Some Admin Portal buttons cannot be understood by screen-reading software
plain.what_happens: The search box and the two small round icon buttons next to it have no names, so software that reads the screen aloud for blind users cannot say what they do.
plain.expected: Every control has a spoken name.
